report.source_text: Subsequent excision of a nodular tumor formation, measuring 3.5 × 3 × 1.5 cm, revealed a neoplasm with firm consistency on section. Macroscopically, the lobulated and grayish skin displayed hemorrhagic foci. Microscopic examination, as depicted in Fig. 2, unveiled a tumor proliferation infiltrating the tendon, arranged in lobules demarcated by fibrous septa. The tumor cells, frequently epithelioid in appearance, exhibited small dimensions, ovoid irregularly outlined nuclei with nucleolar prominence, and pale eosinophilic cytoplasm with occasional clearing. The stroma exhibited fibroinflammatory characteristics and is devoid of epidermal involvement. Additionally, vascular emboli or necrotic foci were not observed.

report.source_text: The patient subsequently underwent metatarsal amputation for definitive treatment. At the 12-month follow-up after metatarsal amputation, the patient remains disease-free with no signs of recurrent or metastatic disease, indicating a favorable clinical course (Table 1).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 25-year-old Moroccan man presented with a mass on his second toe, initially diagnosed as malignant melanoma based on biopsy. This initial diagnosis was a misdiagnosis due to limitations in biopsy analysis (exclusion of epidermis due to artifacting) and absence of immunohistochemical analysis. Eighteen months later, the lesion recurred, prompting re-evaluation. A subsequent excision revealed a nodular tumor with microscopic examination showing a neoplasm infiltrating the tendon, arranged in lobules, with epithelioid cells and pale eosinophilic cytoplasm, and crucially, devoid of epidermal involvement. Immunohistochemical analysis showed positive staining for Melan-A, PS100, HMB-45, and SOX9. Based on these findings, a definitive diagnosis of clear cell sarcoma of soft tissue was established, effectively differentiating it from malignant melanoma. The patient underwent metatarsal amputation and remained disease-free at 12-month follow-up.
